The Erasmus edition of the Greek New Testament, published in 1516, was the first published Greek New Testament and the first printed book to contain the entire New Testament in Greek. It was also the first published edition to use the division of the New Testament into chapters, which was later adopted in many other editions. The first and second edition texts did not include the passage (1 John 5:7–8) that has become known as the Comma Johanneum.
